## Ethical & Scope Disclaimer

This document was produced by **Kernel-X Research Toolkit**, an *observational*
security-analysis instrument intended for academic study, defensive hardening
and audit documentation. Its outputs are derived exclusively from static
telemetry, publicly published advisories and in-process simulations.

The toolkit is **not** an exploitation framework. It contains no exploit code,
performs no memory access (`/dev/mem`, `/dev/kmem`, ptrace) and issues no
commands against hardware-backed security services (KeyMint/keystore2,
Gatekeeper, Weaver). All "simulation" results describe *modelled* behaviour of
documented Android/Linux security boundaries; they do not constitute,
endorse, or assist unauthorised access to any device or account.

Research described here must comply with applicable law and institutional
policy (e.g., ACM/IEEE code of ethics, CFAA/EU Directive 2013/40/EU, and your
IRB/ethics-board approval). Only assess systems you own or have explicit,
written authorisation to test, and follow coordinated-disclosure timelines when
reporting real vulnerabilities. Findings herein are *correlation-based
candidates*; verify against vendor changelogs before disclosure or publication.

metadata.scoring_model: CVSS3.1-impact x reachability x exploit-maturity x applicability x patch-decay, complement-aggregated, mitigation-adjusted

recommendations: Track the latest Android Security Bulletin and OTA baseline; patch age is the single strongest predictor of aggregate kernel exposure.
Prioritize monitoring/verification for the highest-contributing subsystems: core-mm-numa, core-mm-pipe, ebpf-verifier, exynos-lpa.
Verify the 2022-03 (Dirty Pipe) fix is present in the running kernel build via the vendor changelog rather than the version string alone.
Prefer builds that replace legacy ION with dma-buf heaps and constrain heap access with SELinux genfs contexts.
Set kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1 (or 2 on >= 5.8) and restrict BPF program loading to trusted domains.
Re-lock the bootloader for production evaluation units: an unlocked device invalidates AVB trust assumptions across the whole assessment.
Restore/verify the AVB chain-of-trust (vbmeta digest, rollback protection indexes) before drawing conclusions about boot-path integrity.
All findings are *candidates* derived from static version/config correlation; confirm each via vendor source changelogs before publication.
